title: Lanekeeper deployment rituals and checkpad (micro-window) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working-run doc for the 'Lanekeeper' micro-window deployment pattern. Intention is to capture the rituals (preflight, canary ramp, telemetry checks, fallback), a compact hour-by-hour calendar for the rollout day, a short release-notes draft to hand to docs/CS, and a minimal post-deploy checklist.

Context / constraints:
- Target audience: release conductor, on-call stewards, SRE shift, and the feature owner.
- Low-risk micro-window: <5% traffic canary, progressive 3-step ramp, 60m total open window.
- Must preserve latency SLOs (p95 < 180ms) and error budget thresholds.
- Quick rollback path: toggle routing layer -> scale down new variant -> re-route to previous pinned model.

Preflight (T-48h to T-1h) 
- T-48h: Sanity: ensure release branch has green e2e and smoke. Link: GitHub PR/234.
- T-24h: Confirm canary infra reservation (RE-1842) and node quotas with infra.
- T-12h: Run traffic dry-run in staging using the lanekeeper traffic shim (10m, 10k tokens). Check KV cache warmup behavior.
- T-6h: Confirm alerting plays (p95, error-rate, token-cost delta). Owners: Marco (alerts), Evelyn (telemetry queries).
- T-1h: Readout in #release-lanekeeper-ops: quick note with thumbs from SRE + feature owner.

Hour-by-hour rollout calendar (Day D) - Compact 60m window
- D 00:00 - 00:10 (Canary 1): route 1% traffic -> smoke and latency probes, manual verifier on-call.
  - Smoke checklist: basic request/response, edge auth, streaming integrity.
  - Telemetry quick checks: p95 latency, 5xx count, token rate.
- D 00:10 - 00:25 (Canary 2): route 5% traffic -> run longer synthetic chat sequences (30s avg), monitor cost delta.
- D 00:25 - 00:45 (Gradual): route 15% -> observe user-facing metrics + sampling of outputs (quality audit).
- D 00:45 - 01:00 (Decision window): either full open (if all green) or backout to previous routing.

Decision criteria (fast pass = green / amber / red):
- Green: p95 within baseline + error-rate < 0.05% increase + manual quality sampling OK.
- Amber: minor latency bump (p95 + up to 10%), elevated but non-critical errors — hold and extend canary by 30m, assign action owner.
- Red: p95 > baseline + 20% OR new 5xx spike > threshold OR quality regression flagged by eval harness => immediate rollback.

Release notes (hand-off draft to Docs / CS - short form)
- Title: Lanekeeper: incremental routing for model v2026.2
- Summary: Small, controlled rollout of model variant v2026.2 with latency optimizations and updated tokenization fixes. Initial exposure limited via micro-window to mitigate risk.
- Key changes:
  - Reduced attention memory overhead for long context sequences (expected p95 improvement for >1024 tokens).
  - Tokenizer fallback fix for certain emoji sequences (edge-case user prompts).
  - Minor tweak to KV cache eviction to lower memory churn.
- Impact: Most customers unaffected; customers on pinned dedicated pools see no change. Hosted API customers may see improved latency for long sequences.
- Known issues: Intermittent small increase in cold-start latency if GPU provisioning path is exercised (tracked in JIRA RE-1879).
- Rollback: Immediate routing rollback to v2026.1 available; no schema changes.

Post-deploy checklist (first 24h)
- 0–30m: Confirm no sustained increase in 5xx; confirm p95 and p99.
- 30–120m: Run quality sampling on 100 produced responses (mix of chat + long-context). Tag any regressions in RE-1879.
- 6h: Cost snapshot vs baseline (token cost per 1k requests) and note anomalies.
- 24h: Finalize release notes and mark canary closed if stable.

Rollback quick commands (cheat-sheet)
- Routing toggle (infra): /ops route revert --to v2026.1 --reason "rollback: <short reason>"
- Kill new variant pool (if stuck): /infra pools scale --id lanekeeper-v2026.2 --replicas 0
- Reopen canary after fix: follow preflight T-6h checks.

Observability pointers (queries to run)
- Latency: telemetry query "api.latency.p95{route:lanekeeper} by 1m"
- Errors: "sum(rate(api.errors{route:lanekeeper}[5m])) by code"
- Output quality sampling: run eval harness subset "lanekeeper-smoke-100" and review score distribution.

Staffing snapshot (recommended)
- Release conductor: Asha (lead)
- SRE steward: Marco (alert triage)
- Feature owner: Evelyn (quality decisions)
- On-call infra: Liam (node / quota / routing)
- Backup: rotate one additional engineer for quick takeover (T-30m).

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Do we want to bake an automated canary-extension if amber but trending to green? (pros/cons)
- Consider a short-lived sampling job to automatically capture 1% of chat responses and surface anomalies to the UI team.
- Follow up: add a small playbook for when KV cache thrash is observed (notes in Confluence page).

Appendix: quick links
- Runbook: Confluence (linked above)
- PR: GitHub PR/234 (contains deploy manifests and feature flags)
- Incidents: JIRA RE-1879 (tracking cold-start spike)

=== end of draft ===

Notes: This is intentionally compact — copy relevant sections into the canonical runbook if this micro-window becomes standard for more teams. Keep the hand-off release notes short and action-oriented for CS.
